changes: Backlog reached a record $78bn (call), up $5.9bn on the quarter and about $38bn (96%) on the year, with growth in all three segments. Book-to-bill was about 1.3x (derived), down from about 1.5x in 2Q.
Lead times moved out again: large gas prime engine orders now run to 2029 and turbines into 2030, against 'late 2028' in August. 58% of backlog ships within 12 months (59% in 2Q).

Margin is flat underneath: adjusted operating margin excluding tariff refunds was about 20.0%, the same as 2Q. Power & Energy margin was 24.4% (24.6% in 2Q); price of $216mn was mostly offset by capacity costs.
Guide held, 2027 deferred to January. 4Q sales are guided to 'moderate' growth; the FY range implies $19.1bn to $21.8bn. Shares fell 7.6% to $658.90 by 10:17 ET.
Customers are paying earlier: customer advances added $1.4bn of cash in the quarter, while inventories rose $1.6bn to $22.2bn.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Caterpillar as the diversified way into AI data center power: gas gensets and Solar turbines sold years out, capacity rising toward nearly 3x 2024 for large engines, and revenue of about $79.6bn in FY26 and $88.7bn in FY27, with credit not in debate.
headline: The consensus view holds but should stop paying for upside to 2026: demand and backlog keep growing, yet Caterpillar is capacity-bound and margin is flat once tariff refunds are removed, so the case now rests on 2027 capacity and pricing that management will frame only in January; credit quality holds.
kona: Caterpillar now books large gas prime engines into 2029 and turbines into 2030, but smaller gensets have much shorter lead times, some diesel slots are still open in 2028, and management says capacity is fungible across uses. At tens of MW, Kona should design around smaller units sourced through dealers and rental fleets rather than queue for large engines, and budget for deposits: Caterpillar's customer advances rose $1.4bn in the quarter. OEM vendor financing remains a precedent to ask for, but Cat Financial's allowance rose 13% in the quarter, so Kona should not plan on it.

Less or dropped: No updated prime power GW (asked; not given). The 2030 Power Generation 'more than 3x 2024' target was not repeated. The backlog dollar figure was given on the call, not in the release. KPIs more important: Book-to-bill, backlog conversion (58% within 12 months), customer advances, capacity added per quarter. Risks up: 4Q and 2027 estimate risk; freight and energy cost inflation; production ramp (brief test outage, large mining trucks); Cat Financial allowance up 13% QoQ. Risks down: Customer deferrals (none reported); tariff cost ($600mn in 4Q, about $200mn lower YoY); restructuring cut to about $300mn.

sections.body: Caterpillar funds its own growth. MP&E free cash flow of $9.5bn in 9M covered capex and most of the $9.9bn returned to shareholders; buybacks slowed to $1.2bn in 3Q after $6.5bn in H1. Customers are funding part of the build: customer advances added $4.0bn of cash in 9M, against $1.6bn a year earlier. Cat Financial is match-funded and its debt barely moved. No dated bond price or rating action was found today, so no spread is quoted. The next dollar for capacity comes from operating cash and customer deposits, not debt.

sections.body: Signals: 1) Backlog and book-to-bill in 4Q (bar: backlog above $78bn; book-to-bill above 1.0x). 2) FY27 guide in January: sales growth vs the 6-9% CAGR target, margin off the bottom of the band. 3) Power & Energy margin above 24.6% once capacity depreciation is in the base. 4) Customer advances vs inventories: deposits still outrunning inventory build. 5) Cat Financial allowance and any disclosure of data center developer lending. Risks building: Estimate cuts for 4Q; capacity costs absorbing price; Cat Financial allowance rising while past dues are flat. Confirmation: Backlog keeps growing while 58% or more converts within 12 months; 10 MW units ship in 4Q; FY27 margin guide above FY26. Tripwires: Backlog falls QoQ in P&E; a named data center deferral or cancellation; P&E margin below 22%; vendor financing losses.
